questions.q: In the circular flow of income, which of the following is an injection into the Nigerian economy?
options: Company taxes paid to the government
Government spending on a new road in Enugu
Household saving with a commercial bank
questions.explanation: Government spending on a new road adds to the flow of income and is an injection. Household saving, taxes and import payments are leakages because they withdraw purchasing power from the domestic circular flow.

questions.q: A country's real GDP rises from ₦450 billion to ₦495 billion while its population rises from 15 million to 16.5 million. What happens to its real per capita income?
questions.explanation: Initial real per capita income is ₦450 billion ÷ 15 million = ₦30,000, and final real per capita income is ₦495 billion ÷ 16.5 million = ₦30,000. Since both GDP and population rise by 10 per cent, real per capita income stays the same.

questions.q: Which criticism best applies to using per capita income to compare the welfare of Nigerians with that of Ghanaians?
options: It ignores the total population of each country.
It does not show how income is distributed among the people.
It excludes government expenditure from national income.
It cannot be expressed in a common currency.
questions.explanation: Per capita income is an average and can hide wide differences between rich and poor within a country. It uses population and can be converted into a common currency, so the other criticisms do not apply.

questions.q: Cement firms in Ogun State avoid price cuts because each expects rivals to match a cut but ignore a price increase. This behaviour is best explained by...
questions.explanation: The kinked demand curve model explains why oligopolists may keep prices stable: a price cut is matched and brings little gain, while a price increase is not followed and loses customers. This fits the expected reaction described.

questions.q: In the short run, the supply curve of a firm under perfect competition is its marginal cost curve above the minimum point of...
questions.explanation: A perfectly competitive firm will produce in the short run only if price covers average variable cost; the part of marginal cost above minimum average variable cost therefore gives its supply curve. Average fixed cost continues to fall with output and does not determine shut-down.

questions.q: A group of cement producers in Nigeria agree to restrict total output and share the market among themselves. This agreement is an example of...
questions.explanation: A cartel is a formal or informal agreement among competing firms to limit output and divide the market, usually to raise price and profit. A merger combines firms into one, while a natural monopoly arises from large economies of scale rather than an output-sharing agreement.

questions.q: A large textile firm in Kaduna expands output beyond its optimum size and its long-run average cost begins to rise mainly because of...
options: managerial and coordination difficulties associated with large-scale organisation
bulk purchase discounts on raw materials
questions.explanation: Beyond the optimum scale, a firm may suffer diseconomies of scale, such as slower decision-making and difficult coordination, which raise long-run average cost. Bulk discounts, specialisation and better machinery would normally lower cost rather than raise it.

questions.q: A firm's total cost function is TC = 5,000 + 20Q, where TC is in naira and Q is output. What is the marginal cost of producing the 101st unit?
questions.explanation: Total cost at 100 units is 5,000 + 20 × 100 = ₦7,000, and at 101 units it is 5,000 + 20 × 101 = ₦7,020. The additional cost of the 101st unit is ₦7,020 − ₦7,000 = ₦20.

questions.q: A Nigerian importer brings in 2,000 bicycles at ₦45,000 each. If the government imposes a 20% ad valorem tariff, total tariff revenue is...
questions.explanation: The value of the bicycles is 2,000 × ₦45,000 = ₦90,000,000. A 20% ad valorem tariff is 20% of ₦90,000,000, which equals ₦18,000,000.

questions.q: In a market in Makurdi, the demand and supply functions for yams are Qd = 180 − 4P and Qs = 20 + 6P. What are the equilibrium price and quantity?
questions.explanation: At equilibrium, Qd = Qs, so 180 − 4P = 20 + 6P. Solving gives 160 = 10P, hence P = ₦16. Substituting into either function gives Q = 116 units.

questions.q: During a recession, the Federal Government of Nigeria reduces company income tax rates in order to raise aggregate demand. This measure is an example of
questions.explanation: Reducing company income tax is a fiscal policy measure because it involves taxation and government finance. It is expansionary because it can leave firms with more after-tax profit, encouraging investment and raising aggregate demand.

questions.q: The National Planning Commission of Nigeria was mainly established to
options: collect customs duties on imported goods
prepare and coordinate national development plans and advise on plan targets
issue legal tender currency to the public
fix the retail prices of essential commodities
questions.explanation: The commission is concerned with planning, coordination and policy advice on national development. Issuing currency is the role of the Central Bank, customs duties are collected by the customs service, and retail price fixing is not its main function.

questions.q: The demand and supply functions for rice in a local market are Qd = 240 − 8P and Qs = 60 + 4P. If the government fixes the price at ₦10 per unit, what is the resulting market situation?
questions.explanation: At ₦10, quantity demanded is 240 − 8(10) = 160 units, while quantity supplied is 60 + 4(10) = 100 units. Since quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied, there is a shortage of 160 − 100 = 60 units.

questions.q: A state government includes in its budget the payment of salaries and allowances to primary school teachers. In public finance, this item is classified as
questions.explanation: Recurrent expenditure covers routine costs such as wages, salaries, allowances, stationery and maintenance. Teacher salaries are paid for services rendered and are therefore recurrent expenditure, not capital formation or a transfer payment.

questions.q: At the end of a state development plan period, a committee compares actual achievements with the plan targets and examines the causes of any differences. This exercise is best described as
questions.explanation: Evaluation assesses the performance of a development plan by comparing actual results with stated targets. Formulation is the drafting stage, financing deals with funds, and coordination harmonises activities.

questions.q: A decrease in the price of kerosene, which is used together with cooking stoves, will most likely cause
options: a movement down along the demand curve for cooking stoves
a decrease in the demand for cooking stoves
an increase in the supply of cooking stoves
an increase in the demand for cooking stoves
questions.explanation: Kerosene and cooking stoves are complementary goods. When kerosene becomes cheaper, people are more willing to use stoves, so the demand for stoves increases and its demand curve shifts to the right.

questions.q: Amina receives a monthly pension of ₦150,000 when the consumer price index is 125. When the index rises to 150, what is her real monthly pension measured in base-year naira?
questions.explanation: Real income = nominal income × 100 ÷ current price index = ₦150,000 × 100 ÷ 150 = ₦100,000. The figure ₦120,000 would be the real pension at the earlier index of 125, not at the new index.

questions.q: The price of a tin of milk in Kaduna rises from ₦1,200 to ₦1,500, and a shop's quantity demanded falls from 500 tins to 400 tins per month. Using the original values as the base, the price elasticity of demand (ignoring the negative sign) is
questions.explanation: Percentage fall in quantity demanded = 100 ÷ 500 × 100 = 20%, and percentage rise in price = 300 ÷ 1,200 × 100 = 25%. Ignoring the negative sign, elasticity = 20% ÷ 25% = 0.8, which means demand is inelastic.

questions.q: Bola's monthly income rises from ₦100,000 to ₦120,000, and her monthly purchase of bread rises from 40 loaves to 46 loaves. Her income elasticity of demand for bread is
questions.explanation: Income elasticity = percentage change in quantity demanded ÷ percentage change in income. Quantity rises by 6 ÷ 40 × 100 = 15%, while income rises by ₦20,000 ÷ ₦100,000 × 100 = 20%, so the elasticity is 15% ÷ 20% = 0.75.

questions.q: A 5% fall in the price of bread in Ibadan causes the quantity demanded of butter to rise by 2%. The cross elasticity of demand for butter with respect to the price of bread is
questions.explanation: Cross elasticity is the percentage change in quantity demanded of butter divided by the percentage change in the price of bread: +2% ÷ (-5%) = -0.4. The negative value shows that bread and butter are complements.

questions.q: Nyanya in Nasarawa State has a population of 90,000 people living in an area of 1,500 km². What is the population density?
questions.explanation: Population density = total population ÷ land area = 90,000 ÷ 1,500 = 60 persons per km². This measures how closely people are concentrated in the area.

questions.q: A bank in Lagos replaces several cashiers with automated teller machines, and the affected cashiers lose their jobs. This type of unemployment is best described as
questions.explanation: Technological unemployment results when workers are displaced by new machines or production methods. Frictional unemployment occurs between jobs, seasonal unemployment is due to changes in seasons, and cyclical unemployment follows a fall in aggregate demand.

questions.q: A taxi driver in Abuja earns total revenue of ₦45,000 per day and incurs explicit costs of ₦38,000 per day. If he could earn ₦10,000 per day driving for a ride-hailing company instead, his economic profit from operating his own taxi is
questions.explanation: Economic profit subtracts both explicit costs and implicit costs from total revenue: ₦45,000 − ₦38,000 − ₦10,000 = −₦3,000, which is a loss of ₦3,000. The ₦7,000 figure is only the accounting profit, since it ignores the foregone income.

questions.q: A paint factory in Lagos currently has marginal revenue of ₦350 and marginal cost of ₦280 at its present output. To increase profit, the firm should
options: shut down immediately to avoid making a loss
keep output unchanged because revenue is greater than cost
reduce output until marginal revenue equals marginal cost
increase output until marginal revenue equals marginal cost
questions.explanation: When marginal revenue exceeds marginal cost, producing an additional unit adds more to revenue than to cost, so profit rises as output expands. The firm should continue increasing output until marginal revenue equals marginal cost.

questions.q: Which body is responsible for regulating insurance companies in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: The National Insurance Commission is the regulatory authority for insurance business in Nigeria. The Nigeria Deposit Insurance Corporation insures bank deposits, while the Central Bank regulates banks and the Securities and Exchange Commission oversees the capital market.

questions.q: A trader in Aba obtains a bank loan using his landed property as security. If he fails to repay the loan, the bank may sell the property to recover the debt. The property is best described as...
questions.explanation: Property pledged as security for a loan is called collateral, and the lender may dispose of it if the borrower defaults. A premium is an insurance payment, a dividend is a share of profit paid to shareholders, and share capital is money contributed by owners of a company.

questions.q: The price of a close substitute for Dangote cement rises in Onitsha. According to the theory of demand, what will most likely happen to the demand for Dangote cement, other things being equal?
options: It will decrease at each price.
It will increase at each price.
It will increase only when supply also increases.
questions.explanation: When the price of a close substitute rises, consumers tend to switch from the substitute to Dangote cement, so demand for Dangote cement increases at every price. This is a rightward shift of the demand curve, not a movement along it, and it does not require supply to increase first.

questions.q: Rabi's monthly income rises from ₦50,000 to ₦60,000, and her monthly purchases of sachet water rise from 40 to 44 sachets. Using the initial-value percentage method, her income elasticity of demand is...
questions.explanation: Percentage change in quantity demanded = (44 − 40)/40 × 100 = 10%, and percentage change in income = (₦60,000 − ₦50,000)/₦50,000 × 100 = 20%. Income elasticity = 10% ÷ 20% = 0.5, which is positive and less than one.

questions.q: A consumer's money income rises from ₦40,000 to ₦80,000 while the prices of all the goods she buys also double. Her real income will...
questions.explanation: Real income measures the purchasing power of money income, so it depends on income relative to prices. Since both money income and all relevant prices double, the consumer can buy exactly the same quantity of goods as before, meaning real income remains unchanged.

questions.q: In a given year, households save ₦300 billion, firms invest ₦250 billion, government collects taxes of ₦180 billion and spends ₦230 billion, while imports are ₦120 billion and exports are ₦100 billion. What is the net injection into the circular flow of income?
questions.explanation: Injections are investment, government spending and exports: ₦250 billion + ₦230 billion + ₦100 billion = ₦580 billion. Leakages are savings, taxes and imports: ₦300 billion + ₦180 billion + ₦120 billion = ₦600 billion. Since leakages exceed injections by ₦20 billion, the circular flow experiences a net withdrawal of ₦20 billion.

questions.q: In calculating Nigeria's Gross Domestic Product by the value-added approach, the value of intermediate goods is excluded mainly to avoid...
questions.explanation: The value-added approach counts only the extra value produced at each stage of production; including intermediate goods as well would count the same output more than once. Double counting would therefore overstate GDP, while depreciation, imports and inflation are separate issues.

questions.q: A state government grants one firm the exclusive right to supply electricity in a town and forbids other firms from entering the market. This type of monopoly is best described as...
questions.explanation: A statutory monopoly arises when the law or government grant gives a single firm the exclusive right to supply a good or service. A natural monopoly results from cost conditions that make one firm the cheapest supplier, while a monopsony is a market with a single buyer and perfect competition has many sellers.

questions.q: A palm-oil processing plant in Ilorin has one fixed press. With 2 workers, it produces 40 drums of oil per day; with 3 workers, 54 drums; and with 4 workers, 64 drums. What is the marginal product of the fourth worker?
questions.explanation: Marginal product is the change in total output caused by adding one more worker. Output rises from 54 drums to 64 drums when the fourth worker is employed, so MP = 64 − 54 = 10 drums. The value 14 drums is the marginal product of the third worker, not the fourth.

questions.q: A garment factory in Kaduna doubles both its labour and capital, and its output rises from 1,200 shirts to 2,700 shirts. This result shows that the firm is experiencing
questions.explanation: Doubling all inputs raises output by more than double, from 1,200 to 2,700 shirts, which is increasing returns to scale. Diminishing marginal returns concerns adding one variable input while at least one factor is fixed, not changing all inputs together.

questions.q: A country’s export price index is 160 while its import price index is 125, with the base year equal to 100. What is the country’s terms of trade?
questions.explanation: Terms of trade = (export price index ÷ import price index) × 100 = (160 ÷ 125) × 100 = 128. The value 35 is merely the difference between the two index numbers.

questions.q: Which of the following transactions will be recorded as a credit item in Nigeria’s current account?
options: A Nigerian firm sells cocoa to a Dutch buyer
Nigeria pays interest on a loan obtained from a foreign bank
A Nigerian importer pays for vehicles bought from Japan
A Nigerian student pays tuition fees to a university in Canada
questions.explanation: A sale of cocoa abroad is an export of goods and brings foreign exchange into Nigeria, so it is entered as a credit in the current account. Payments for imported vehicles, foreign tuition, and interest on foreign loans are outflows and are debited.

questions.q: A state government in Nigeria finances a rural development programme with a foreign loan that must be repaid with interest. What is the most direct future economic burden created by this method of financing?
options: The total removal of opportunity cost
A permanent surplus in the current account
Future interest and principal repayments abroad
An automatic appreciation of the naira
questions.explanation: Borrowing from abroad creates future repayment obligations, including interest and principal, which must be met in foreign exchange. Loan inflows do not permanently improve the current account, remove opportunity cost, or automatically raise the value of the naira.

questions.q: The demand function for a commodity is Qd = 120 − 4P. Using the point elasticity formula and the negative sign convention, what is the price elasticity of demand when P = 10?
questions.explanation: At P = 10, Qd = 120 − 4(10) = 80. Point elasticity is (dQd/dP) × (P/Qd) = (−4) × (10/80) = −0.5.

questions.q: A government sets a minimum price for maize above the equilibrium price. What is the most likely effect in the maize market if the price is strictly enforced?
options: A movement of the demand curve to the left
A surplus, because quantity supplied exceeds quantity demanded
A shortage, because quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied
An immediate fall in the market price to equilibrium
questions.explanation: A minimum price above equilibrium prevents the price from falling to equilibrium, so producers supply more than consumers are willing to buy, creating a surplus. A shortage would arise from a maximum price set below equilibrium.

questions.q: The establishment of a tomato processing factory in Kano near tomato farms is most likely to
options: increase the importation of tomato paste into Nigeria
shift labour from agriculture to petroleum refining
reduce post-harvest losses and provide a ready market for tomato farmers
discourage farmers from adopting better storage methods
questions.explanation: Locating a processing factory near farms turns perishable tomatoes into paste, reducing spoilage and creating demand for farmers' produce. Importation, discouraging storage, and shifting labour to petroleum refining are not direct effects of such a processing investment.

questions.q: Which of the following measures would most directly improve agricultural productivity in Nigeria?
options: reducing farmers' access to rural credit
regular supply of improved inputs and extension services
increasing the number of middlemen in the marketing chain
questions.explanation: Improved seeds, fertiliser and extension advice raise output per hectare and help farmers adopt better methods. More middlemen or less credit do not raise farm productivity, while reliance only on rain-fed farming increases risk from irregular rainfall.

questions.q: A budget in which estimated government revenue is greater than estimated government expenditure is called a
questions.explanation: A surplus budget occurs when estimated revenue exceeds estimated expenditure. A balanced budget has equal revenue and expenditure, while a deficit budget has expenditure greater than revenue; a supplementary budget is an additional appropriation, not a revenue-expenditure relationship.

questions.q: Which of the following taxes is regressive in effect?
options: a fixed annual trade licence fee of ₦2,000 paid by every trader
a tax rate that rises as taxable income rises
a higher tax rate on luxury cars
questions.explanation: A fixed licence fee takes a larger share of a low earner's income than of a high earner's income, so it is regressive in effect. A uniform percentage tax on all incomes is proportional, while a rate that rises with income and a higher tax on luxury cars are progressive.

questions.q: Which fiscal policy measure is most appropriate to reduce demand-pull inflation in Nigeria?
options: reduce taxes while maintaining government expenditure
reduce taxes and increase government expenditure
increase taxes and reduce government expenditure
increase government expenditure without raising taxes
questions.explanation: Demand-pull inflation is reduced by contracting aggregate demand, which can be done by raising taxes and cutting government spending. Lowering taxes or raising spending would usually increase aggregate demand and worsen the pressure on prices.

questions.q: If the consumer price index rises from 120 to 150 in a year, the rate of inflation for that year is
questions.explanation: Inflation rate = [(150 − 120) ÷ 120] × 100 = 25%. The calculation does not yield 30%, 20% or 12.5%.

questions.q: The price elasticity of demand for a commodity is 2.5. If its price rises by 10%, the quantity demanded will
questions.explanation: Price elasticity of demand = percentage change in quantity demanded ÷ percentage change in price, ignoring the negative sign. Here, 2.5 = %ΔQ ÷ 10, so %ΔQ = 25%, and a price rise causes quantity demanded to fall.

questions.q: A demand curve that is vertical at every price indicates that demand is
questions.explanation: A vertical demand curve shows that the same quantity is demanded at every price, so quantity demanded does not respond to price changes. The coefficient of elasticity is zero, meaning demand is perfectly inelastic.

questions.q: Which of the following situations best illustrates the economic concept of scarcity?
options: A trader in Aba has more cartons of shoes than customers demand at the current price.
A community in Niger State enjoys fresh air without paying for it.
A farmer in Oyo State harvests more yam than he can store.
A student in Jos wants to buy a new textbook but has only enough money for either the textbook or a school bag.
questions.explanation: Scarcity exists when limited resources cannot satisfy all wants. The student has limited money and must choose between the textbook and the school bag, which illustrates scarcity and choice. The situations involving unsold shoes, fresh air and excess yam describe a surplus or a free good rather than scarcity.

questions.q: If both the demand for and supply of sachet water in Enugu increase at the same time, what is the certain effect on the market equilibrium?
questions.explanation: A rightward shift in demand raises equilibrium quantity, and a rightward shift in supply also raises equilibrium quantity. Therefore quantity sold must rise, while the effect on price is uncertain because the two shifts push price in opposite directions.

questions.q: Which of the following is a fixed cost of a bread bakery in the short run?
options: Monthly rent for the bakery building
Fuel used to run the oven
questions.explanation: A fixed cost does not change with the level of output in the short run. Monthly rent for the bakery building is payable even when no bread is baked, while flour, casual wages and oven fuel are variable costs.

questions.q: A caterer in Enugu earns total revenue of ₦180,000 in a month. Her explicit costs are ₦135,000, and she could earn ₦30,000 as a salaried employee elsewhere in the same month. What is her economic profit?
questions.explanation: Economic profit subtracts both explicit and implicit costs from total revenue. Explicit-cost profit is ₦180,000 − ₦135,000 = ₦45,000, and subtracting the ₦30,000 forgone salary gives ₦15,000. The ₦45,000 figure is only accounting profit, while ₦75,000 wrongly adds the implicit cost.

questions.q: A printing press in Kaduna has total fixed cost of ₦45,000. At an output of 1,500 exercise books, its total variable cost is ₦105,000. What is its average total cost per exercise book?
questions.explanation: Total cost is fixed cost plus variable cost, that is ₦45,000 + ₦105,000 = ₦150,000. Average total cost is ₦150,000 ÷ 1,500 = ₦100 per exercise book. The ₦30 and ₦70 figures are average fixed cost and average variable cost respectively.

questions.q: A trained nurse from Ibadan moves to Canada to take up a nursing job. This movement is best described as:
questions.explanation: Geographical mobility refers to the movement of labour from one place or country to another. The nurse changes location but continues in the same occupation, so this is not occupational mobility; vertical and seasonal mobility refer to different ideas.

questions.q: Chief Ade in Lagos needs an account that allows him to write cheques to suppliers and make many withdrawals during the week. Which type of account is most suitable?
questions.explanation: A current account is designed for frequent transactions and permits the account holder to use cheques. Savings accounts are mainly for deposits, fixed deposits restrict withdrawals, and a domiciliary account is held in a foreign currency rather than serving the stated general purpose.

questions.q: Which of the following is a factor income in the calculation of Nigeria's national income?
options: Pension paid to a retired civil servant
Money received from the sale of a used car
Rent received by a landlord for a factory building
Monthly allowance paid by a father to his son in university
questions.explanation: Rent received for a factory building is earned by land as a factor of production, so it is included in national income as factor income. The allowance and pension are transfer payments, while the proceeds from a private sale of a used car do not represent newly produced goods in the period.

questions.q: In an economy, households spend ₦520 billion on consumption, firms spend ₦140 billion on investment, government spends ₦95 billion, exports are ₦80 billion and imports are ₦110 billion. Using the expenditure approach, GDP at market prices is
questions.explanation: GDP by expenditure is C + I + G + (X − M) = ₦520b + ₦140b + ₦95b + (₦80b − ₦110b) = ₦725 billion. Adding imports instead of subtracting them gives ₦945 billion, so that value is not GDP.

questions.q: Compared with a perfectly competitive industry with the same costs, a profit-maximising monopoly will most likely
options: charge a higher price and sell a smaller quantity
produce where price equals marginal cost
charge a lower price and sell a larger quantity
earn only normal profit in the long run
questions.explanation: A profit-maximising monopoly sets output where marginal revenue equals marginal cost and charges the price on the demand curve, which is above marginal cost. A perfectly competitive industry sets price equal to marginal cost, giving a lower price and larger output, so the monopoly charges more and sells less.

questions.q: A monopolist faces the demand curve P = 100 − 2Q and has a total cost function TC = 20Q. What output maximises profit?
questions.explanation: Profit is maximised where marginal revenue equals marginal cost. Total revenue is 100Q − 2Q², so MR = 100 − 4Q; with MC = 20, setting 100 − 4Q = 20 gives Q = 20 units.

questions.q: A small shoe factory in Aba produces 200 pairs of shoes with 6 workers. When a seventh worker is employed, total output rises to 245 pairs. The marginal product of the seventh worker is
questions.explanation: Marginal product is the addition to total output from employing one more worker: 245 pairs − 200 pairs = 45 pairs. Dividing total output by the number of workers gives average product, which would be 35 pairs for seven workers.

questions.q: When the total product of a variable input reaches its maximum, the marginal product of that input is
questions.explanation: The total product is maximum where an additional unit of the variable input adds nothing to output, so marginal product is zero. Once marginal product becomes negative, total product falls.
